fields.sections.0.h: Immediate Reinstatement Announcement and Government Involvement
fields.sections.1.h: Genesis of the Infidelity Incident and Resignation
fields.sections.2.h: Government Review and National Security Conclusion
fields.sections.4.h: Stock Rebound and Tech Leaders' Lobbying
fields.sections.5.h: Investigation Continues and Interim CEO Role
fields.sections.6.h: Congressional Scrutiny and Export Control Debate Reopened
fields.sections.0.ko: The Nvidia board announced the immediate reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO. The board specified that it had solicited views from senior U.S. federal government officials in this decision-making process and determined that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk. This represents a dramatic reversal approximately 10 days after his resignation due to an infidelity scandal on November 13.
fields.sections.1.ko: Huang resigned after multiple infidelity allegations were reported in early November, with one woman having been identified as having contacts with a Chinese government intelligence operative, escalating the matter into a national security issue. According to New York Times reporting, the woman (Alice Huang) was in contact with a Chinese State Security Ministry official during at least part of her relationship with Huang. Huang self-disclosed one instance of infidelity in a letter to employees.
fields.sections.2.ko: According to government officials who requested anonymity, senior officials provided a briefing to the Nvidia board last week and notified them that no national security laws were violated. This news prompted the board to resume contact with Huang. Reinstatement was decided at a second meeting on Sunday following the first face-to-face meeting on Saturday, with the sharp decline in Nvidia's stock price estimated to have accelerated the negotiation process.
fields.sections.3.ko: President Donald Trump communicated directly and indirectly with the Nvidia board in a Monday CNBC interview and claimed that Huang had done nothing wrong. Trump disclosed that he spoke with Huang on Sunday and requested that he promise to work hard. After reinstatement, Trump posted on social media that the board's decision was correct and that Huang's leadership is necessary for U.S. economic success and Nvidia's prosperity. He also described Huang as a "great patriot and national treasure."
fields.sections.4.ko: Following news of Huang's reinstatement, Nvidia's stock price rose 31%. This represents a substantial recovery from a roughly 33% decline since November 8 when Huang acknowledged infidelity. Major tech leaders including Elon Musk, Gavin Baker, and Brad Gerstner actively advocated for Huang's reinstatement, with Musk declaring on social media that the board's mistake had been corrected.
fields.sections.5.ko: The Nvidia board had continued to insist last week that it would not consider Huang's reinstatement but reversed course sharply. The board will retain Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, whom it had appointed as interim CEO, and has decided to hire an external law firm to conduct an independent investigation into whether Huang and security violations occurred. Huang committed to cooperating sincerely with this investigation.
fields.sections.6.ko: Despite Huang's reinstatement, the U.S. Congress intends to intensively investigate Nvidia's chip sales to China and Southeast Asia and its security compliance. Senator Elizabeth Warren stated that the reinstatement decision does not dispel national security suspicions. Huang has been the most vocal opponent of advanced chip export restrictions, and lawmakers intend to investigate whether the fact that his infidelity partner was an intelligence operative influenced his export control stance.
fields.sections.7.ko: Huang has been summoned for a closed-door House Foreign Affairs Committee recorded testimony on December 1 and a public Senate Finance Committee testimony on December 3. Senate Finance Committee Chairman Tim Scott formalized that Huang will attend as the sole witness and testify at a hearing on protecting U.S. AI superiority and export control oversight. Senator Andy Kim pointed out that answers are needed regarding what Nvidia and the Trump administration knew and what adequate measures were taken to prevent critical technology leakage.
fields.caveat: This article is stated to have been written in November 2026, which is a future event compared to the current timepoint (2025), so please verify whether this represents an actual event or a hypothetical scenario before referencing.
